alignment.note: The Syriac conjunction and noun are fused in ܘܫܐܕܐ, so this index also carries the demon-noun shared with Greek δαιμόνια and Latin dæmonia.

Greek ἐξέβαλλον and Latin ejiciebant render the durative imperfect with a single finite verb; the Peshitta expresses the same continuous past with a periphrastic participle plus auxiliary ܡܦܩܝܢ ܗܘܘ, the standard Syriac iterative-past construction.
The Syriac proclitic waw on ܘܡܫܚܝܢ corresponds to the conjunction καί / et beginning the second clause.
Greek ἤλειφον and Latin ungebant use a simple imperfect; the Peshitta again employs the periphrastic ܡܫܚܝܢ ܗܘܘ to mark continuous past action, a syntactic divergence without semantic effect.
Greek dative ἐλαίῳ and Latin ablative oleo express instrument by case; Syriac marks the same instrumental sense with the preposition ܒ prefixed to ܡܫܚܐ.

Greek πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους and Latin multos ægros place the quantifier before the noun, whereas Syriac inverts the order to ܟܪܝܗܐ ܣܓܝܐܐ ('sick many'), reflecting the normal Syriac noun-adjective sequence.

Greek ἐθεράπευον and Latin sanabant use a finite imperfect; the Peshitta renders the healing with the periphrastic ܡܐܣܝܢ ܗܘܘ, consistent with its pattern of marking habitual past action throughout this verse.
